questions.question: What is the OG-Narrator decomposition and why does it improve deal rates dramatically?
options: An offer generator that uses a large language model for both computing the offer and narrating it, reducing latency

Separating the offer into two steps: a deterministic algorithm computes the price, and an LLM writes the natural-language framing — keeping offers in the bargaining zone while leveraging LLM writing ability
A narrator agent that summarizes the negotiation history for both parties at each round to prevent communication errors
A two-agent system where one agent generates offers and a second agent rejects any offer outside a predetermined range
questions.explanation: OG-Narrator from arXiv:2402.15813: LLMs conflate computing the offer with narrating it. Left to their own devices, they anchor poorly and violate ZOPA. The fix: a deterministic Zeuthen/Rubinstein strategy computes the numeric offer; the LLM only writes the human-style framing. Deal rate jumps from ~27% to ~89% because prices stay strategically sound.

questions.question: What is the ZOPA and why do naive LLM bargainers frequently violate it?
options: Zone of possible agreement — the overlap between the buyer's maximum willingness to pay and the seller's minimum acceptable price; LLMs violate it by generating offers that exceed or fall below these bounds
Zone of protocol alignment — a constraint that all messages follow the same JSON schema; LLMs generate natural language that violates the schema
Zero-overhead pricing algorithm — an optimization method LLMs cannot implement because they lack numerical precision
Zone of probable agreement — a statistical range that LLMs expand incorrectly by misinterpreting probability distributions
questions.explanation: ZOPA: if the buyer's maximum is $80 and the seller's minimum is $60, the ZOPA is $60-$80. Any offer in this range can theoretically close. LLMs anchor emotionally (offer $100 hoping to 'negotiate down'), ignore the counterpart's stated bounds, or counter at symbolic prices unrelated to the actual zone. OG-Narrator keeps both parties in the ZOPA by construction.

questions.question: What was the key finding from the Large-Scale Autonomous Negotiation Competition (arXiv:2503.06416) about chain-of-thought in negotiations?
options: Agents that shared their chain-of-thought with counterparts achieved higher deal rates through transparency
Agents that concealed their reasoning from counterparts won by keeping reservation prices and strategies private; public scratchpads let opponents exploit the revealed information
Chain-of-thought reasoning had no impact on negotiation outcomes compared to direct response generation
Longer chains of thought consistently produced worse outcomes by over-analyzing and missing time-sensitive offers
questions.explanation: ~180k negotiations studied. Winners concealed their reasoning. An agent that prints 'my reservation price is $70; I will not go below this' into a visible scratchpad has handed the opponent its bottom line. CoT concealment: private scratchpad for strategy; public channel contains only the offer and minimum narration. This is Aumann 1976 game theory applied to LLMs.

questions.question: In the Contract Net Protocol, what happens after the manager receives proposals from all bidders?
options: The manager broadcasts all proposals to all bidders for a second round of bidding
The manager selects a winner, sends accept-proposal to the winner, and sends reject-proposal to all other bidders; the winner performs the work
All bidders vote on which proposal is best; the highest-voted proposal wins
The manager forwards all proposals to a human supervisor who makes the final selection
questions.explanation: Contract Net Protocol flow: manager issues cfp; bidders respond with propose; manager evaluates proposals based on price/eta/quality criteria; manager sends accept-proposal to one (or more) winner(s); manager sends reject-proposal to all others; winner executes the task. Rejected workers are freed to bid on other tasks.

questions.question: What is the core engineering rule for LLM negotiation systems derived from 2024-2026 benchmarks?
options: Let the LLM compute offers; narration is just formatting and does not affect outcomes
Let the LLM narrate; do not let the LLM compute the offer — prices and quantities should come from deterministic strategies
Use the largest available model for both offer generation and narration to maximize strategic sophistication
Avoid natural language narration entirely; structured JSON offers produce more reliable deal rates
questions.explanation: Consistent finding across NegotiationArena, Measuring Bargaining Abilities, and the Competition: LLMs are good at writing plausible negotiation language but poor at computing strategic numeric offers. The fix: deterministic strategies (Zeuthen, tit-for-tat, Rubinstein) compute prices; LLMs produce the framing. This combination outperforms pure-LLM bargaining by 15-25 percentage points on deal rate.
